question: In a rheumatoid arthritis study utilizing bulk rna seq, An analyst takes the top 200 differentially expressed genes from a targeted microfluidic panel (500 genes total) and performs Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) against the entire human genome (20,000 genes) in MSigDB. How should this analysis be evaluated and executed?
proposed_analysis: Proposed analysis: An analyst takes the top 200 differentially expressed genes from a targeted microfluidic panel (500 genes total) and performs Over-Representation Analysis (ORA) against the entire human genome (20,000 genes) in MSigDB.
preferred_analysis: ORA background must strictly reflect the tested gene universe (the 500 panel genes). Using the whole genome artificially inflates overlap significance for pathway genes present on the targeted panel.
reasoning_summary: Rigorous scientific assessment for rheumatoid_arthritis: ORA background must strictly reflect the tested gene universe (the 500 panel genes). Using the whole genome artificially inflates overlap significance for pathway genes present on the targeted panel.

supported_claims.statement: Experimental data for rheumatoid_arthritis was generated under specified assay parameters.

unsupported_claims.statement: The flawed analysis proves generalizable mechanism in rheumatoid_arthritis.

limitations: Methodological validity requires rigorous control of uncalibrated_ora_background.
